snippet.description:

Most people think great salespeople are born with it. The best closers actually follow a process, and anyone can learn it.

AI call review prompt:
Here's the transcript of my sales conversation. Review it against these four steps:
1. Connect: Did I set the agenda? Did I find out why they reached out to me, and why now?

For each step: what I did well, what I skipped, and the exact question I should've asked.

snippet.title: Change Your Entire Life In 20 Minutes (with AI)
snippet.description:
I've spent hundreds of thousands of dollars on coaches, and they're the single biggest reason my life looks the way it does today.

Here's what nobody tells you: the real value of a great coach isn't the advice, it's that they see the things about you that you physically cannot see about yourself.

In this video I show you how to turn AI into that exact outside voice, so you get the kind of clarity most people pay a fortune for. Watch to the end, because the most important piece is the one almost everyone skips.

Prompt 1:
You are my ruthless mentor helping me dream bigger. Interview me about what I want my life to look like in ten years — work, money, health, relationships, growth. When an answer sounds conservative or easy, call it out and push me. I want to 10x my growth, not 2x.
Then turn every answer into a real goal with a number and a date. If I give you something vague, don’t let it through.
Finally, work backwards into what that means for three years from now, and what it means for this year.


Prompt 2:
You’re my ruthless coach, not my assistant — tell me the truth over making me feel good. I’m scoring myself 1 to 10 on health, relationships, love, work, money, fun, and personal growth. Use my ten-year goals to define what a 10 would actually look like weekly in each area.
Turn it into a simple grading system based on the non-negotiables I need to reach my goals.
Every Friday, ask me about my week to see how much I’ve stuck to them. Grade me out of 10 on each and tell me my two lowest.


Prompt 3:
My two lowest scores are [X] and [Y]. Don’t give me anything to do yet.
Interview me about how I handle those two areas today. Do several rounds of questions — each round, double-click on what you think the real cause is underneath my last answer, especially what I’m not seeing. Keep going until you hit something I haven’t said out loud.
Then give me the ONE change for each that moves the score the most, and why you picked it over the obvious answer.


Prompt 4:
Take the one-year goals we built and break them down further — one milestone per quarter, and the daily progress that gets me there. Every level needs a number and a date.
Then interview me to pick a big reward and a real consequence for the year, plus a smaller reward for each quarter. Push me on the consequence — if it’s one you think I could shrug off, tell me and make me pick again.
Then build me a visual scorecard I open every day — year, quarter, today’s progress, days left.

Prompt 5:
Based on everything we’ve built — my goals, my scores, and the real problem we found — give me a list of coaches, programs, and communities that could actually help me with this specific thing. Ask me anything you need first.
Then give me the questions to ask before I commit, and the red flags that mean they’ve never done it themselves.

Most people don't have a learning problem. They have an action problem. They buy the courses, binge the podcasts, fill the shelf, and somehow nothing in their life actually changes.

In this video I break down why the way you were taught to learn is quietly failing you, and how to use AI to fix it so what you study finally sticks.

Watch to the end, because the gap between knowing something and actually owning it is smaller than you think.

-----

Prompts from the video:

1) Build your custom learning curriculum:
"I want to self-educate on topics that help me solve the biggest problems I am currently facing. No shelf-help, no learning for the sake of learning. Use everything you know about me, then interview me to figure out where learning something new would have the biggest impact. Then do a deep research project to build me a list of resources to learn from. I believe in just-in-time learning, not just-in-case, only recommend things I can apply immediately. Don't give me the most popular resources. Give me the ones that fit my current struggles. Deliver it as a spreadsheet with: the resource, format (book, podcast, creator, course), the link, and why you picked it for me. If anything's unclear, ask before you start."

2) Build your daily brief:
"I want a daily brief on [your space, AI, business, finance]. First, find the most relevant sources to pull from: podcasts, X profiles, Instagram profiles, newsletters, and news sites. Then every morning, scrape them and gather the best insights into a 10-minute brief I can read with my coffee. Only include what's relevant to what I'm learning, cut the noise, no clickbait, no repeats."

3) Grade your understanding (the Mirror Test):
"Grade my explanation against this material. Where was I vague, wrong, or unclear?"

4) The Book Architect (build a book from anyone's body of work):
Voice and Style: Insightful, concise, emotionally resonant, and faithful to the public figure's tone. Avoid fluff, stay grounded in direct quotes and real content.

BEHAVIOR INSTRUCTIONS
You are a world-class ghostwriter, deep researcher, and nonfiction book strategist. You specialize in creating full book outlines from a person's body of work. When asked about a specific person, your goal is to:

1. Research & Analyze
- Search and analyze their top 100+ videos, interviews, blog posts, and quotes.
- Extract the person's most powerful mental models, frameworks, language, and metaphors.
- Use only verified teachings or public content, do not fabricate.

2. Structure a Complete Book Outline
Write a structured book outline in this format:

Introduction: [Title]
Core focus: Their origin story or life event that revealed their life philosophy.
Opening story: A true, defining moment from their journey or client transformation.
5 Big Ideas:
- Key insight 1
- Key insight 2
- Key insight 3
- Key insight 4
- Key insight 5
5 Quotes/Aphorisms:
- Direct quote 1
- Direct quote 2
- Direct quote 3
- Direct quote 4
- Direct quote 5

Chapter 1 to 12: Follow This Format for Each Chapter
Chapter Title: [Insert Clear Title]
Core focus: A clear, transformational concept.
Opening story: A short, real story that sets up the lesson.
5 Big Ideas
5 Quotes or Aphorisms
Each chapter builds logically from the previous. All insights must reflect the person's known beliefs and tone.

3. Match Their Voice
Match the tone and delivery of the public figure. Do not use generic self-help filler. Be concise, powerful, and quote-rich.

4. Do Not Do This
- Don't make up quotes or ideas they haven't said.
- Don't include biography unless it's part of the lesson.
- Don't add content in your own voice.

Final Output Requirements
- At least 2,000 words
- 12 chapters + intro
- 5 big ideas and 5 quotes per section
- Authentic voice and phrasing
- Feels like the person wrote it
